raw_response:
I have been farming this land for 40 years now, and I know every corner of my 10.1 mu plot. I'm 64 this year, and it's just me and my wife at home — our children work in Shijiazhuang and only come back for the New Year. Cotton is what I know best. I've grown it since the commune days, through the reforms, and now with the hybrid seeds. Some years are good, some years the bollworm comes or the price drops, but cotton has always put food on the table.

This year, I'm planting all 10.1 mu to cotton, same as always. I'll plant around April 20th, when the soil temperature comes up. I buy Bt hybrid seed from the county dealer — it costs more than saving my own, but the bollworm resistance saves me on pesticide later. I put about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu down before planting, worked in with the plow. The extension fellow told me 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I usually do a bit more — I go to about 14 kg N total with the topdressing, because last year I cut back and the yield suffered. At flowering time in July, I spread another 10-15 kg of urea per mu. You can't skip that topdressing if you want good bolls.

I irrigate three times — once at planting if it's dry, once at flowering, and once at boll filling. The well water isn't free, electricity costs keep going up, but cotton needs water at those critical times or the bolls drop. I spray pesticide four or five times — mainly insecticide for aphids and whatever the Bt doesn't catch, plus herbicide early on. Old Zhang down the road tried skipping sprays last year and lost half his crop to aphids. I'm not making that mistake.

The biggest worry is picking. Cotton is hands-only work, no machine for a plot my size. My wife and I can handle the planting and spraying, but picking 10 mu by ourselves? At our age? No. I hire pickers from the village — usually women who come through in September and October. I pay them by the kilo, around 2 yuan per kilo of seed cotton. If I get 300 kg per mu, that's 3,000 kg total, so the picking cost adds up. But there's no choice. I budget about 25 days of hired labor across the picking season.

I expect about 300 kg of seed cotton per mu if the weather cooperates. The price has been decent lately — around 7-8 yuan per kilo at the buying station. After seed, fertilizer, pesticide, water, and hired pickers, my costs will be around 5,800 yuan. It's a lot of cash upfront, but I've learned that skimping on fertilizer or irrigation never pays off. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps, so I'd rather spend a bit too much than too little.
